Remove redundant assertion from the inline `active_value()`. ## Overview
This PR introduces a performance optimization to fix a visual glitch that occurs when a player first starts a level. Previously, the browser would not fetch the directional robot PNGs (up, down, left, right) until the exact moment the user pressed the corresponding key, resulting in a momentary flicker or "invisible robot" effect as the asset downloaded.

- Network tab confirms sprites are fetched and cached prior to user input.

Wildcard Western used vertical stacked text-button lists for player selection and display, causing overflow and requiring scroll on mobile. This update replaces those lists with compact wrapped circular avatar grids consistent with the repo's existing houseguest avatar patterns, and also adds spectator-flow and duel-feedback polish requested in PR feedback.

## New components

**`WwAvatar`** — self-contained circular avatar with western-themed visual states:
- `isSelected` → gold ring + glow
- `isDuelist` → pulsing western-gold keyframe animation
- `isEliminated` → grayscale + red ✕ overlay
- `isYou` → "YOU" badge
- `size`: `sm` (36px) / `md` (68px) / `lg` (80px)
- Uses the repo-standard avatar fallback chain: `resolveAvatar()` → DiceBear → initials fallback if image loading still fails

**`WwAvatarDuelist`** — non-interactive `lg` avatar for VS pair displays; highlights the buzzed player with gold ring + 🎯 badge

## Phases updated

| Phase | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cardReveal` | text name on card | circular avatar above card value |
| `pairIntro` / `finalDuel` | plain text names | `WwAvatarDuelist` VS pair |
| `duelQuestion` / `buzzOpen` / `answerOpen` | plain text names | duelist avatars; buzzed player highlighted |

- **Avatar resilience**: completed the image fallback path so failed primary and DiceBear loads still render accessible initials instead of a broken avatar
- **Non-interactive avatar semantics**: duel-display/status avatars that are not clickable no longer render as buttons
- **Spectator modal accessibility**:
  - focus now moves into the dialog when it opens
  - the dialog is labeled with `aria-labelledby` / `aria-describedby`
  - Escape and backdrop dismissal safely resolve to continue-watching behavior
- **CSS cleanup**:
  - consolidated duplicate `.ww-duel-pair` styling
  - removed unused `.ww-duel-avatar-name` CSS

- ✅ `npm run test`

All underlying game rules, phase logic, AI planners, timer guards, and idempotency safeguards remain intact. The added spectator flow and duel feedback are component-level UX improvements layered on top of the existing gameplay behavior.

## Summary
- fix Telegram approval handling so request id `0` is treated as valid instead of being auto-cancelled
- keep rejecting blank approval ids on Telegram to avoid creating unrecoverable pending approvals
- share backend approval-request normalization across Telegram and Discord so id/turn parsing semantics stay aligned

Telegram and Discord were normalizing app-server approval requests separately. Telegram treated `message["id"] == 0` as falsy and returned `"cancel"` before surfacing an approval prompt. body:
Multiple microservices write to the shared `request_logger_request` table with no way to distinguish which service produced each row. Instead of adding a column to identify the service, each service can now use its own prefixed tables by passing a `table_prefix` parameter at startup.

### Changes

- **`request_logger/utils.py`**: Added `resolve_table_name()` helper with regex validation to safely build prefixed table names. Updated `save_request()` to use `psycopg.sql.SQL` + `psycopg.sql.Identifier` for dynamic table names.
- **`request_logger/services.py`**: Added `table_prefix` parameter to `database_request_logger_middleware()` and `DatabaseRequestLoggerMiddleware.__init__()`, passed through both success and error paths.
- **`rate_limiter/services.py`**: Added `table_prefix` parameter to `rate_limiter_middleware()` and `RateLimiterMiddleware.__init__()`, since the rate limiter reads from the same `request_logger_request` table for counting.
- **`rate_limiter/utils.py`**: Updated `assert_capacity()`, `fetch_rate_limiter_rule()`, `fetch_rate_limiter_count()`, and all three time-period count functions to accept `table_prefix` and use safe SQL composition for both `request_logger_request` and `rate_limiter_rule` tables.
- **`test_table_prefix.py`**: 18 unit tests covering `resolve_table_name`, middleware wiring for both middlewares, `save_request` SQL generation, and prefix input validation.

### Usage

```python
# Both middlewares should use the same prefix so the rate limiter
# counts requests from the correct prefixed table.
```

author: iclanton
body:
## Summary

Improves the reliability of pipeline runs by pinning the Rush version used by `install-run-rush.js` to a validated lockfile, preventing unexpected Rush upgrades from breaking CI.

- Adds `INSTALL_RUN_RUSH_LOCKFILE_PATH` support to the `install-run-rush.yaml` pipeline template, pointing to a checked-in lockfile at `common/config/validation/rush-package-lock.json`.
- Adds a `RepoPath` parameter to the template (defaults to `$(Build.SourcesDirectory)`) so callers with non-default checkout paths can specify the repo root; it drives both `workingDirectory` and the lockfile path.
- Updates all pipeline templates and the GitHub Actions CI workflow to use the new template parameter.
- Updates `BumpDecoupledLocalDependencies` to regenerate `rush-package-lock.json` as part of the automated decoupled dependency bump PR.

## Details

`install-run-rush.js` respects the `INSTALL_RUN_RUSH_LOCKFILE_PATH` environment variable to pin the npm install of the Rush version to a specific lockfile. Previously this was not set, so Rush could be silently upgraded (or downgraded) between runs. The new template sets it unconditionally.

The `RepoPath` parameter was needed because the post-publish pipeline checks out a second repo (`rushstackWebsites`) into a non-default directory; without it, the `workingDirectory` and lockfile path would point at the wrong location.

`BumpDecoupledLocalDependencies` now copies the Rush package lockfile into `common/config/validation/rush-package-lock.json` after running `rush update`, keeping the pinned version in sync with the rest of the repo's dependency updates.

## How it was tested

Reviewed pipeline template changes manually and confirmed that all callers pass through the new `RepoPath` parameter where needed. The `rush-package-lock.json` content was generated by running `rush update` locally.

body:
Admin auth token was held only in React state, so every page reload dropped the session and forced re-authentication.

## Changes

- **Token persistence**: `useState` lazy initializer reads from `sessionStorage` on mount; token is written to `sessionStorage` on successful login and removed on logout.
- **Auto-authentication**: Mount-only `useEffect` (guarded by an `autoAuthRan` ref) validates any stored token against the API on load — auto-signs in if valid, clears stale token and surfaces `admin_login_error` if rejected.
- **Shared `validateToken` helper**: Extracted `useCallback` used by both `handleLogin` and the auto-auth effect to avoid duplicated fetch logic.

```ts
// Token survives reload
const [token, setToken] = useState(() => sessionStorage.getItem("adminToken") ?? "");

// Validated and auto-authenticated on mount
useEffect(() => {
  if (autoAuthRan.current || !token || isAuthenticated) return;
  autoAuthRan.current = true;
  validateToken(token)
    .then((valid) => { /* set authenticated or clear stale token */ });
}, [token, isAuthenticated, validateToken]);
```

`sessionStorage` is intentional — persists across reloads within the tab, but is cleared automatically when the tab/browser is closed.

### Related Issue

**Issue:** #XXXX

### Description

This fixes cache token telemetry inconsistencies for OpenRouter-compatible providers (OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, and Cline proxy paths).

What was happening:
- OpenRouter reported cache writes via `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` and we handled that in `OpenRouterHandler`.
- Vercel AI Gateway commonly reports cache writes via `cache_creation_input_tokens` instead, so `cacheWriteTokens` stayed at `0`.
- Cline handler had the same issue in streaming usage parsing.

What changed:
- Added a shared parser: `extractCacheTokenUsage()` in `src/core/api/providers/cache-usage.ts`.
- It normalizes cache usage fields from multiple response shapes:
  - `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`
  - `prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`
  - `cache_read_input_tokens`
  - `cache_creation_input_tokens`
  - `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`
  - `prompt_cache_miss_tokens`
- Wired the parser into:
  - `OpenRouterHandler`
  - `VercelAIGatewayHandler`
  - `ClineHandler`
- Updated non-cached input token calculation to consistently compute:
  - `prompt_tokens - cacheReadTokens - cacheWriteTokens`

At /apps/my-cool-app, it finds the apps route via pathname.startsWith(r.path) and shows Home > Apps — the :appName param is ignored. The fix: make the breadcrumb parse all path segments, resolve params against route data, and support a useBreadcrumb context so pages can inject dynamic labels (e.g., the actual app name).

Phase 1 — Breadcrumb Context for Dynamic Labels
Create BreadcrumbContext — New file frontend/src/hooks/useBreadcrumb.ts:
Context holds a Map<string, string> of path-segment overrides (e.g., { "my-cool-app": "My Cool App" })
useBreadcrumbLabel(segment: string, label: string) — hook that registers a dynamic label on mount and clears on unmount. Pages call this to inject entity names.
useBreadcrumbOverrides() — consumed by Breadcrumb.tsx to resolve dynamic labels
Provider wraps the app in AppLayout.tsx (alongside existing providers)
Wire provider — In frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx, wrap content with <BreadcrumbProvider>. Depends on step 1.
Phase 2 — Rewrite Breadcrumb Component
Rewrite Breadcrumb.tsx — In frontend/src/layout/Breadcrumb.tsx:
Split pathname into segments: /apps/my-cool-app → ["apps", "my-cool-app"]
For each segment, build cumulative path: apps, /apps/my-cool-app
Resolve label: first check BreadcrumbContext overrides, then check NAV_ROUTES lookup (keyed by path), then fallback to decodeURIComponent(segment) title-cased
Render N segments (not capped at 2): Home > Apps > My Cool App
Last segment remains non-interactive (<span>), all prior segments are <Link>
Keep existing styling (ChevronRight separator, text-muted-foreground, hover effects)
Depends on step 1.
Phase 3 — Pages Register Dynamic Labels
AppsPage — In frontend/src/pages/AppsPage.tsx:
When appName param exists, call useBreadcrumbLabel(appName, app.display_name ?? appName) using the fetched app data. This makes /apps/my-cool-app render as Home > Apps > My Cool App.
The label cleans up automatically on unmount (navigating away).
Depends on steps 1, 3.
Any future parameterized routes (e.g., /activity/:eventId, /pipeline/:pipelineId) can call useBreadcrumbLabel() in the same pattern. No changes to the breadcrumb component needed — it's generic. Parallel with step 4.
Phase 4 — Handle Edge Cases
Trailing slashes — Strip trailing slashes from pathname before splitting. Part of step 3.
Unknown segments — If a segment doesn't match NAV_ROUTES and has no context override, display it as title-cased decoded URI (e.g., my-cool-app → My Cool App). Part of step 3.
404 routes — The catch-all * route maps to NotFoundPage. Breadcrumb should show Home > Not Found or just Home. The current behavior of falling back to "Home" alone is fine. Part of step 3.
/help and /settings — No params, no change — they continue to show 2-segment breadcrumbs as before. No action.
Relevant Files
File	Action
frontend/src/hooks/useBreadcrumb.ts	New — BreadcrumbContext + useBreadcrumbLabel hook
frontend/src/layout/Breadcrumb.tsx	Rewrite to parse all path segments + consume context overrides
frontend/src/layout/AppLayout.tsx	Wrap with <BreadcrumbProvider>
frontend/src/pages/AppsPage.tsx	Call useBreadcrumbLabel(appName, displayName)
frontend/src/constants.ts	Reference: NAV_ROUTES array (no change, used as lookup)
Verification
apps → shows Home > Apps (unchanged)
/apps/my-cool-app → shows Home > Apps > My Cool App (new third crumb with app display name)
Click "Apps" crumb at /apps/my-cool-app → navigates to apps list view
Navigate away from /apps/my-cool-app → dynamic label cleaned up from context, no stale crumbs
Unknown deep path (e.g., manually typed /apps/nonexistent) → shows Home > Apps > Nonexistent (title-cased fallback) until data loads or 404 renders
All flat routes (/projects, /pipeline, /agents, etc.) → unchanged 2-segment breadcrumbs
/ (home) → shows only Home (unchanged)
Run Vitest to confirm no regressions
Decisions
Context-based over react-router handle metadata — avoids coupling breadcrumb labels to route definitions and supports async data (entity names from API responses)
Fallback to title-cased segment — ensures breadcrumb never shows raw URL slugs like "my-cool-app"; renders "My Cool App" even before API data loads
No NAV_ROUTES restructuring — the flat array stays as-is; breadcrumb path...

author: nakatamaho
body:
**Summary**

In `SLAQP2RK`, `DLAQP2RK`, `CLAQP2RK`, and `ZLAQP2RK`, the argument `KMAX` is documented as `[in]`, but the implementation overwrites it:

```fortran
KMAX = MIN( KMAX, MINMNFACT )
```

This is a contradiction between the documentation and the implementation.

**Root cause**

Fortran callers are insulated from this side effect because `DGEQP3RK` (and its variants) pass a temporary expression `JMAX - J + 1` rather than a named variable, so the write to `KMAX` inside `xLAQP2RK` is silently discarded. However:

- The `[in]` annotation is violated.
- C and C++ translations of these routines fail to compile, since an rvalue cannot be bound to a non-const reference.
- Any caller that passes a named variable directly (e.g., in testing or alternative driver routines) will have that variable silently corrupted.

**Fix**

Introduce a local variable `KBOUND` to hold the clamped value. `KMAX` is no longer written to.

```fortran
-      KMAX = MIN( KMAX, MINMNFACT )
-      DO KK = 1, KMAX
+      KBOUND = MIN( KMAX, MINMNFACT )
+      DO KK = 1, KBOUND
 ...
-      K = KMAX
+      K = KBOUND
```

**Files changed**

- `SRC/slaqp2rk.f`
- `SRC/dlaqp2rk.f`
- `SRC/claqp2rk.f`
- `SRC/zlaqp2rk.f`

**No behavior change**

The computed result is identical for all existing callers. This is a correctness fix for the argument intent annotation and a robustness fix for non-Fortran consumers of these routines.

body:
Closes #235

## Summary

- `PUT /v1/working-memory/{session_id}` accepts `user_id` and `namespace` in the **request body**, embedding them into the Redis key (e.g. `working_memory:demo:alice:session-1`)
- `GET` and `DELETE` take those values as **query params**, which default to `None` when omitted, producing a different key (`working_memory:session-1`) — resulting in a 404
- This adds an index-based fallback: when a direct key lookup returns nothing, the existing working memory search index is queried by `session_id` to resolve the actual Redis key
- Multi-tenant isolation is preserved (namespace/user_id remain in keys); the fallback only fires when the direct lookup misses

## Changes

- **`working_memory.py`**: Add `_resolve_working_memory_key_via_index()` helper; wire fallback into `get_working_memory()` and `delete_working_memory()`; return stored `namespace`/`user_id` from the JSON document instead of caller-supplied params
- **`mcp.py`**: Add missing `user_id` and `namespace` parameters to the MCP `get_working_memory` tool
- **`tests/test_issue_235.py`**: 9 tests covering key resolution, API round-trips, delete without params, multi-tenant isolation, and non-existent session handling

## Test plan

- [x] `test_get_resolves_via_index_when_params_omitted` — PUT with scoping params, GET without → 200
- [x] `test_get_with_partial_params_resolves` — GET with namespace only still resolves
- [x] `test_get_with_correct_params_still_uses_fast_path` — direct lookup still works when params match
- [x] `test_delete_resolves_via_index_when_params_omitted` — DELETE without params removes the correct session
- [x] `test_api_put_body_params_get_without_query_params` — full HTTP round-trip
- [x] `test_api_delete_without_query_params` — full HTTP DELETE round-trip
- [x] `test_multi_tenant_isolation_preserved` — same session_id in different namespaces stays separate
- [x] `test_nonexistent_session_still_returns_none` — no false positives
- [x] Full test suite: 781 passed, 105 skipped, 0 failures

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Moderate risk because it changes working-memory GET/DELETE lookup behavior and introduces index-based key resolution that could affect multi-tenant correctness if the search index is stale or filtering is insufficient (though ambiguity is explicitly rejected).
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes working-memory retrieval/deletion when a session was stored with scoped Redis keys (`namespace`/`user_id`) but later fetched/deleted without those parameters by adding an **index-based fallback** that searches the working-memory Redis Search index by `session_id` to resolve the actual key.
> 
> The fallback refuses to return data when the `session_id` is ambiguous across tenants (warns and returns `None`), and `get_working_memory` now returns stored `namespace`/`user_id` from the JSON document when the caller omitted them. The MCP `get_working_memory` tool is updated to accept/pass `user_id` and `namespace`, and a new `tests/test_issue_235.py` covers GET/DELETE/API round-trips plus multi-tenant disambiguation behavior.

## Summary

Complete PRO RC engineering workflow from governing-case provenance through beam continuity elevations, plus PRO verification QA improvements folded in from upstream.

**Stacked on PR [1]** (#39 — La Bombonera fixture).

## What's Included

### Governing-Case Pipeline (Steps A+B)
- `governing-case.ts` — identifies which load combination governs each element per force component (Mz, Vy, N, My, Vz, torsion)
- `auto-verify.ts` — extracted verification utility with governing combo annotation

### PRO Report Combo Context (Step C)
- `pro-report.ts` — load-combinations reference table in model-data section
- `pro-report.ts` — governing combo column in verification summary table
- `ProPanel.svelte` — passes combo definitions to report data

### RC Detailing + Visual Improvements (Step D)
- `cirsoc201.ts` — `DetailingResult` interface + `computeDetailingRules()` per CIRSOC 201 Ch. 12 (ld, ldh, lap splice, min spacing, stirrup hooks)
- `reinforcement-svg.ts` — beam elevation: anchorage tails at supports, splice zone indicators, framing context column stubs, corrected bar Y-positions (bottom bars at bottom, top bars at top), top bar multi-row layout
- `reinforcement-svg.ts` — column elevation: development below foundation, splice zone near base, proportional tie hooks, beam context stubs
- `reinforcement-svg.ts` — splice and detailing labels use i18n via `spliceLabel` parameter
- `cirsoc201.ts` — Z-up `classifyElement()` fix (uses dz as vertical, not dy)
- `cirsoc201.test.ts` — classification tests updated for Z-up

### Joint-Aware Detailing + Beam Continuity (Step E)
- `structural-graph.ts` — pre-computed connectivity graph (node connectivity, beam-column joints, horizontal/vertical frame lines)
- `reinforcement-svg.ts` — upgraded `generateJointDetailSvg()`: detailing-aware hook dimensions (ldh), column splice zone, translated labels, node ID annotation
- `reinforcement-svg.ts` — new `generateFrameLineElevationSvg()`: continuous multi-span beam elevation with bottom bars, top support bars, splice zones, column stubs, end anchorage, span dimensions
- `ProVerificationTab.svelte` — joint details derived from actual model connections (up to 8 unique types), beam continuity section in Detailing tab

### PRO Verification QA (folded in from upstream)
- Manual reinforcement override system (per-element bar count/diameter override)
- Override-aware quantity calculations (adjusted longitudinal rebar weight)
- XLSX rebar schedule export (2-sheet workbook: grouped schedule + quantities)
- Multi-normative code selector (CIRSOC / ACI-AISC / Eurocode / NDS / Masonry / CFS)
- Grouped rebar schedule by identical section + reinforcement pattern
- Verification UI ordering and QA fixes

## New Files

- `web/src/lib/engine/governing-case.ts`
- `web/src/lib/engine/auto-verify.ts`
- `web/src/lib/engine/structural-graph.ts`

## Modified Files

- `cirsoc201.ts`, `cirsoc301.ts`, `cirsoc201.test.ts`
- `results.svelte.ts`, `live-calc.ts`
- `pro-report.ts`, `reinforcement-svg.ts`
- `ProPanel.svelte`, `ProVerificationTab.svelte`
- `en.ts`, `es.ts` (i18n keys for detailing, joints, continuity, overrides, schedule)

## Validation

- All CI checks pass: lint ✓, test ✓ (22m), web ✓
- `npm run build` passes locally
- No solver/engine code touched

## Known Limitations (v1)

- Positive-moment assumption for bottom bars (no moment-sign intelligence)
- Frame-line tracing is greedy (T-intersections may split)
- Column-stack continuity not yet implemented
- Report does not yet include beam continuity elevations or upgraded joints
- Serviceability checks (crack/deflection) are computed but not yet rendered
